newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Japan's Akihito lands in Rio to wrap up Brazil trip.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Akihito lands in Rio to wrap up Brazil trip.

text.p: Japanese Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko on Sunday landed in the tourist mecca of Rio de Janeiro, on the last leg of a 10-day Brazil tour that has taken them from the Amazon to the country's chilly south.

The imperial couple arrived amid tight security at an air force base at Rio's Galeao International Airport shortly after midday (1500 GMT) after spending a day and a half in the southern state of Parana, an air force official said.
On the first Japanese imperial visit to Latin America, Akihito and Michiko will spend 24 hours in Rio before travelling on Monday to Buenos Aires for a three-day visit to Argentina.

They were received at Galeao by a cheering crowd and Rio's state governor and archbishop before being whisked to city hall, where they were to be greeted by members of Rio's Japanese-Brazilian colony and treated to a samba dance exhibition.
They also will visit the city's famed Botanical Garden and end the day with a meeting with Gov. Marcello Alencar at the state house, known as Palacio Larangeiras.
On Monday, the imperial couple will visit a social centre before boarding a flight to Buenos Aires.

Akihito and Michiko began their visit to Brazil on May 31 with a trip to the Amazon at Belem port where the river flows into the Atlantic, then dined with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in Brasilia.

They spent two days in industrial Sao Paulo, home to most of the 1.3 million Brazilians of Japanese descent, before travelling to Parana's capital of Curitiba, where the second-largest colony of Japanese-Brazilians live.
Despite tight security, the couple thrilled fans in both cities and were greeted by the traditional Japanese patriotic cry of "Banzai!"
Brazil is home to the largest Japanese community outside of Japan.
